notes: Independent live ranking-evidence pass for all 14 candidates: ten discovery journals and four diamond additions. Only difficulty, metrics and per-record audit notes are supplied; route/fees, formats, review and scope fields are not replaced.

Difficulty bands are provisional agent judgments within the relevant public-policy specialty, not a cross-disciplinary prestige order or manuscript-specific prediction. very_high is reserved here for the three inspected Sage venues reporting aggregate acceptance below 10%; high uses a lower aggregate rate or explicit demanding contribution/selectivity criteria. Unknown is retained where the available evidence establishes review/fit without sufficient comparative selectivity.

Sage defines acceptance over all article types receiving final accept/reject decisions in the previous calendar year. Hence 2025 is derived at the 2026-11-16 check; individual metric pages have no explicit year label. Definition: https://www.sagepub.com/journals/understanding-journal-metrics .

Sage speed values are displayed as medians but their exact reporting periods were not stated on the inspected metrics pages, so they are not included as dated metrics. Rates are not used to forecast author turnaround. JEPP rates/citation data are official indexed evidence with blocked direct access; all such limitations are explicit in its patch.

Non-null officially reported metrics only; missing, undated or period-ambiguous values remain absent from the metrics arrays. Policy Sciences first-decision timing and JDD/JPP undated citation metrics are documented in audit notes rather than assigned invented dates.

Citation impact, readership/downloads and publication counts are separate descriptors and do not determine acceptance difficulty. Cambridge publication categories can overlap; no acceptance rate was reconstructed from counts.

The fee audit was read and its seven needs_verification routes and conditional Cambridge route are not overridden. In particular, the four Sage page-charge holds remain the fee auditor's responsibility. IPR research screening delay and op-ed closure are preserved separately.

This is an independent agent evidence review of public policies, not human scientific review, a venue endorsement, or a fee guarantee. No venue was contacted and no submission, account purchase, publication or remote write occurred.
